items.prompt: Define development.
items.canonical_answer: Improvement in people's quality of life across economic, social, political and environmental dimensions.
marking_guidance: Meaning: improvement in quality of life, covering the economic, social, political and environmental dimensions. Accept a precise equivalent formulation.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: Suggest an improvement to a fictional workshop project that creates paid jobs but discharges untreated waste into the settlement's drinking-water stream. Explain why your change supports development.
items.canonical_answer: Install and maintain a suitable waste-treatment system so jobs can continue while water contamination is reduced. Maintenance and safe disposal are needed for the environmental and health gains to last.
marking_guidance: Context: address the stated contaminated stream.
Reason: connect a feasible waste-control action to safer water while retaining the economic opportunity. Do not require the learner to name a particular treatment technology.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: Describe two different features used to classify world development patterns.
items.canonical_answer: Income-related groupings describe relative economic development. Industrialised and less industrialised describe the importance and capacity of industrial production.
marking_guidance: Feature: identify and describe two distinct classification dimensions; ownership arrangements are also a valid dimension. Do not award a second feature for restating the same income label.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: Describe the distinction between industrialised and less industrialised economies.
items.canonical_answer: An industrialised economy has substantial industrial productive capacity; a less industrialised economy has relatively less. The distinction concerns economic structure rather than the mere presence of a factory.
marking_guidance: Feature: relative industrial capacity or importance, with the distinction clearly paired.

items.prompt: Explain the error when a learner calls a fictional country's GNI per person of N$35,000 its total national income.
items.canonical_answer: The learner has confused an average with a national total. Per person means the national measure has been divided by population; N$35,000 is an average, not the total for the whole country.
marking_guidance: Error: national total confused with per-person average.
Distinction: use the division-by-population test; the average does not mean each individual receives that amount.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: Explain which fictional area should be investigated first for water support if the aim is to improve access: H has annual average income per person N$50,000 and safe-water access 40%; J has N$30,000 and 85%. Weigh an income-only rule against the supplied access evidence.
items.canonical_answer: Investigate H first for the stated aim: only 40% have safe-water access compared with 85% in J. An income-only rule would prioritise J because its average is lower, but that would overlook H's much larger access gap. Average income per person remains useful for economic resources, yet access evidence is more directly relevant to this decision.
marking_guidance: Judgement: a supported priority tied to improving water access.
Reason: weigh the conflicting income and access signals, explaining why the selected evidence fits the aim. Accept a conditional alternative if it genuinely addresses the criterion and both sources.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: State (a) two dimensions of development illustrated by this original fictional case [2]. Explain (b) why the factory's higher output alone does not establish an overall improvement in local development, using both supplied changes [4]. Case: output rises from 100 to 150 bags per week, but safe-water access falls from 80% to 50% after untreated waste enters the community's supply.
items.canonical_answer: (a) Economic and environmental development; social development is also relevant to safe water. (b) Production rises by 50 bags a week, supporting an economic gain, while safe-water access falls by 30 percentage points. The adverse water change means increased output coexists with worse living conditions. Overall improvement cannot be established from output alone; benefits and costs to people must be considered together.
marking_guidance: Point (a), 2 marks: two relevant dimensions, accurately identified.

Development (b), up to 4 marks: use both the output increase and access deterioration to explain the conflict between dimensions and the inadequacy of an output-only conclusion. Reward a connected contrast; a generic list without using the source does not meet the analytical demand.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: Calculate (a) annual GNP per person for fictional Country R, showing working [2]. Explain (b) whether R's larger total GNP is a sound reason to prioritise S for a project whose stated aim is to reduce the share lacking safe water, using the averages and access figures [4]. Original same-year data: R, GNP N$360 million, population 18,000, safe-water access 45%; S, GNP N$240 million, population 8,000, safe-water access 80%. The definitions and currency basis are comparable.
items.canonical_answer: (a) N$360,000,000 ÷ 18,000 = N$20,000 per person per year. (b) No. S has N$30,000 per person per year, so R's larger total actually accompanies a lower average. Moreover, 55% in R lack safe-water access compared with 20% in S. R therefore warrants priority investigation for the stated water aim. The figures establish average resources and access gaps, not final project costs or which particular households need support.
marking_guidance: Evidence (a), 2 marks: accurate division and N$20,000 per person per year.

Meaning (b), up to 4 marks: compare the two averages, use the water-access evidence and give a connected reason for the priority under the stated aim. An income-only assertion or an unsupported recommendation is insufficient. Detailed project feasibility is not supplied; accept a conditional priority consistent with that limit.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.
